title: Review 2024 Census county-water edge leads for 16 California, Oregon and Washington counties
body:
Bounded coordinated evidence follow-up from #487 and #486. Review exactly the 17 source/current neighbor-pair candidates and 16 assigned county-equivalent locations listed below. #487 supplies the California/Washington side (15 locations); #486 supplies Oregon Clatsop. Parent evidence is in #487's and #486's declared packets.

Reproduction lead: a temporary EPSG:5070 shared-boundary graph (1 m minimum shared segment) finds 219 internal pairs from the 2018 geoBoundaries USA ADM2 shapes, 234 from U.S. Census TIGER/Line 2024, and 218 in current Atlas for the 97 assigned county predecessors. The 2018/current set differs by one pair (Alameda–San Francisco); the 2024/current candidate set differs by 17 pairs and current has no extra pair. TIGER 2024 carries county `ALAND`/`AWATER` fields and therefore exposes substantial county-water extents in these coastal pairs. The current footprints are close to the 2018 source in land areas but often exclude or truncate the 2024 source's water-only county edges. This evidence demonstrates a source-vintage/land-water-scope question; it does not establish that the land geography is wrong or authorize a county line move.

Resolve the Alameda–San Francisco source/vintage lead separately. Coordinate the Clatsop–Pacific pair with both source packet owners and the regional integrator. If the evidence shows a shared-location inconsistency, propose one joint bounded engineering follow-up naming all affected locations; do not move shared boundaries or alter hierarchy, geometry, data, certificates or imports in this research task. Insufficient official marine/county line evidence remains an explicit finding.
